newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trade on Monday, dealers said.
"It's a slow afternoon. Liquidity wasn't as tight as initially feared," one local bank dealer said.
Dealers said overnight money fell to 10.0/11.0 percent from a high of 12.0/13.0 percent in the morning.
The local bank dealer said sentiment was rather bearish on the dollar at present because of the slow rupiah depreciation and relatively expensive short-term swaps.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,369/2.561 and the conversion band at 2,369/2,417 on Monday.
The central bank depreciated the rupiah by only two points last week after lowering it by four points the previous week.
The dealer said a slower rupiah depreciation last week, coupled with sustained expensive short-dated swaps, seemed to reduce the attractiveness of going long in dollars.
"The underlying tone seems to favour the rupiah, supported by further concerns on the liquidity outlook," another said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,372.5/73.0 at 0845 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,374.25/74.75.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,371.60/72.00 and 2,71.25/72.15, respectively.
One state bank dealer said liquidity should not be tight on Tuesday because of the weekly tax payments.
"Tax payments are usually smaller at month-ends. But some banks tend to increase their payments before the end of the 1996/97 fiscal year on March 31," she said.
Dealers said other factors affecting liquidity outlook was the upcoming Lunar New Year on February 7 and Eid al-Fitr celebrations on February 9 and 10.
Overnight swap was at 0.45/0.50 and tom/next at 0.53/0.55.
One-month swaps were at 13.00/13.75, two at 23.50/24.50, three at 36.25/37.25 and six at 73.50/74.50 points.
